slides.2.content:
Olfactory Receptors and Neural Transmission

StageMechanismKey ElementsWine Application
1. Volatile ReleaseMolecules volatilise from wine into the nasal cavityTemperature, swirling, alcohol concentrationOptimal temperature enhances aroma release
2. 受體結合氣味分子與嗅覺受體蛋白結合~400 種受體 (人類)複雜香氣需多受體共同識別
3. Signal TransductionGPCR (G Protein-Coupled Receptor) amplifies signalcAMP (cyclic Adenosine Monophosphate) second messengerDetectable at extremely low concentrations (ppt level)
4. 嗅球處理訊號彙集至嗅球 glomeruli空間編碼模式不同香氣產生獨特編碼
5. Brain IntegrationPiriform cortex, amygdala, hippocampusMemory and emotional connectionsAromas trigger regional/varietal associations

Taste Receptor Distribution and Perception

基本味覺受體類型敏感區域葡萄酒中來源閾值
甜味T1R2+T1R3舌尖、軟顎殘糖、甘油0.5~1% (葡萄糖)
AcidityH⁺ ion channelsSides of tongueTartaric acid, malic acidDetectable at pH 3.0
BitternessT2R (25 types)Back of tongueTannins, seed polyphenolsVery low (evolutionary protection mechanism)
SaltinessNa⁺ channelsFront of tongueMinerals (trace)0.05% NaCl
UmamiT1R1+T1R3Whole tongueAmino acids (aged wines)0.01% MSG (Monosodium Glutamate)

Sensory Adaptation and Fatigue

Olfactory Adaptation

  • 快速適應: 持續暴露於同一香氣 30~60 秒後，感知強度下降 50~70%。
  • 受體飽和: 嗅覺受體去敏化，需 3~5 分鐘恢復。
  • Blind Tasting Response:
    • 每款酒間隔 2~3 分鐘，中間聞咖啡豆或自己手臂 (重置嗅覺)。
    • Avoid tasting the same variety consecutively (e.g. 5 Cabernets in a row).
    • Begin with a neutral sample (water, alcohol solution) to calibrate the baseline.

Olfactory fatigue is the greatest enemy of tasting; professional panels evaluate no more than 40–50 wines per day.

Gustatory Fatigue

  • Acid Fatigue: Sensitivity decreases after tasting multiple high-acid wines; rinse with plain water.
  • Tannin Accumulation: Tannins bind with salivary proteins causing astringency; take breaks and eat neutral foods (bread).
  • Alcohol Anaesthesia: High-ABV wines numb the palate; taste in ascending ABV order.
  • 甜味飽和: 甜酒後品干型酒會顯得過酸，需調整順序 (干→甜)。

Standard tasting sequence: Sparkling → White (dry → sweet) → Red (light → full) → Fortified sweet.

跨感官影響 Cross-modal Effects

  • 顏色偏誤: 深色酒被評為更濃郁 (視覺影響味覺)，盲品需用黑色杯或紅光。
  • Temperature Effect: Low temperature suppresses sweetness (+30%) and enhances acidity (+20%); high temperature does the opposite.
  • Sonic Effect: High-frequency sounds enhance sweet perception; low frequency enhances bitterness (avoid noisy environments).
  • Expectation Effect: Knowing the brand/price raises scores by 15–20% (blind tasting eliminates this bias).

Professional tasting rooms require: white light (5000K), 20–22°C, fragrance-free, quiet environment.

Sensory Memory and Training

  • Short-term Sensory Memory: Retains only 3–7 aroma characteristics; record immediately.
  • Long-term Memory Formation: Repeated exposure (10+ times) builds stable aroma–vocabulary associations.
  • Reference Sample Library: Use aroma kits such as Le Nez du Vin to train identification accuracy.
  • Blind Tasting Practice: At least 2 blind tasting sessions per week (3–5 wines); log error patterns and correct them.

Individual Variation and Genetic Influence

Variable FactorEffectPopulation %Tasting Adjustment
TAS2R38 gene10× variation in bitterness sensitivity25% supertastersBitterness scores must be calibrated
OR7D4 geneCannot perceive androstenone~30% anosmicAvoid as a primary descriptor
AgeOlfactory receptors decrease 50% after age 60Ageing effectRecalibrate regularly
SexWomen average 10–15% higher olfactory sensitivityPhysiological differenceBalance panel by sex

slides.3.title: Chapter 2
slides.4.content:
SAT (Systematic Approach to Tasting) Structured Protocol

  1. Visual Assessment (30 s): Clarity, intensity, colour, viscosity, bubbles (if present).
  2. 嗅覺評估 (90 秒): 狀態、強度、發展階段、香氣特徵 (3 層次)。
  3. Gustatory Assessment (60 s): Sweetness, acidity, tannins, alcohol, body, flavour intensity, finish.
  4. Conclusion (30 s): Quality rating, development potential, typicity, region/variety inference.

Systematic Tasting Sheet (SAT)

Assessment ItemScaleKey IndicatorsTypical Descriptors
Appearance IntensityPale / Medium / DeepPigment density, light transmissionPale, Medium, Deep
Aroma IntensityLight / Med– / Med / Med+ / PronouncedDetectable without swirlingLight, Pronounced
AcidityLow / Med– / Med / Med+ / HighSalivation, lateral tongue stimulationLow, High
TanninsLow / Med– / Med / Med+ / HighAstringency intensity, textureFine-grained, Grippy
BodyLight / Med– / Med / Med+ / FullWeight in mouth, viscosityLight, Full-bodied
FinishShort / Med– / Med / Med+ / LongDuration after swallowing (seconds)Short (<3s), Long (>8s)
品質差 / 可接受 / 良好 / 優 / 傑出平衡、複雜度、餘韻Acceptable, Outstanding

Calibration Training Methods

Triangle Test

Purpose: Test evaluators' ability to distinguish subtle differences.

Protocol:

  1. Provide 3 glasses: 2 identical (A) and 1 different (B).
  2. Evaluator must identify which glass differs from the other two.
  3. 隨機猜測正確率 33%，統計顯著需 > 60% (n=20)。

Applications:

  • Test ability to distinguish plots within the same appellation (Pauillac vs St-Julien).
  • 測試是否能區分不同橡木桶處理 (法國桶 vs 美國桶)。
  • Test fault thresholds (e.g. TCA 2 ng/L vs 4 ng/L).

Training tip: conduct a triangle test monthly and track accuracy trends.

Reference Standards Calibration

Purpose: Establish a shared scoring baseline.

Protocol:

  1. Prepare samples of known quality levels (Good, Very Good, Outstanding).
  2. All evaluators score independently.
  3. Compare scores to the reference answers to identify systematic bias.
  4. Adjust individual scoring scale (e.g. if someone systematically underscores by 5 pts).

Reference Sample Examples:

Quality LevelReference WineKey Characteristics
Acceptable (65–69)Basic AC BordeauxFault-free but lacking complexity
Good (70–79)Village-level BurgundyCorrect, balanced, typical
Very Good (80–89)Cru Bourgeois MédocComplex, balanced, finish Med+
Outstanding (90–100)Grand Cru ClasséExceptional complexity and ageing potential

每季度重新校準一次，使用新年份樣品。

Consensus Discussion

目的: 統一描述詞使用與評分標準。

Protocol:

  1. Evaluators independently assess and score the same wine.
  2. Reveal all scores; calculate standard deviation (SD).
  3. If SD > 5 pts, hold a discussion:
    • 高分者說明為何給高分 (複雜度、平衡、餘韻)。
    • Lower scorers explain their deductions (faults, imbalance).
  4. Re-taste and revise scores to reach consensus (SD < 3).

Common Sources of Disagreement:

  • Descriptor Ambiguity: "Earthy" may refer to positive mineral character or negative mouldy notes.
  • Personal Preference: High-acid lovers vs high-alcohol lovers.
  • Experience Gap: Novices and experts have different understandings of "complexity".

Consensus discussion aims not for perfect uniformity, but to reduce unnecessary disagreement.

Scoring Consistency Metrics

MetricCalculationAcceptable StandardApplication
Intraclass Correlation (ICC)Score correlation between evaluatorsICC > 0.75Overall panel reliability
Standard Deviation (SD)Score dispersion for same wineSD < 5 ptsSingle wine consensus
Test-retest ReliabilitySame evaluator retests after 2 weeksr > 0.85Individual stability
Sensitivity (d')Discrimination ability (signal detection theory)d' > 1.5Evaluator screening

Blind Tasting Environment Standardisation

  • 酒杯: ISO 標準杯 (INAO 杯)，容量 210 ml，倒 50 ml。
  • Temperature: White wines 10–12°C, red wines 16–18°C, ±2°C control.
  • Order: Randomise to avoid order effects; use a Latin square design.
  • Coding: Three-digit random codes; avoid leading numbers (e.g. 1, 2, 3).
  • Timing: 10 am–12 pm is optimal (peak sensory acuity).

slides.6.content:
Common Wine Fault Classification

Fault TypeChemical SourceSensory CharacterThresholdOrigin
Cork TaintTCA (2,4,6-trichloroanisole)Damp cardboard, mould, suppressed fruit2–4 ng/LContaminated corks
Volatile AcidityAcetic acid (VA)Vinegar, nail polish remover0.7 g/L (red), 0.6 g/L (white)Acetobacter, Brettanomyces
Brett Contamination4-EP, 4-EGStable, plasters, smoky bacon400–600 μg/LBrettanomyces yeast
ReductionH₂S, mercaptansRotten egg, burnt rubber, garlic1–10 μg/LAnaerobic fermentation, yeast stress
OxidationAcetaldehydeApple cider vinegar, caramel, loss of fruit100–125 mg/LExcessive oxygen exposure
光照劣變硫醇 (光誘導)濕羊毛、煮高麗菜極低UV 光暴露 (透明瓶)
熱傷害美拉德產物煮水果、焦糖化、平板N/A高溫儲存 (>25°C)

Fault Identification Training Kit

TCA (Cork Taint)

Chemistry: 2,4,6-trichloroanisole; extremely low threshold (2–4 ng/L = ppt level).

Sensory Description:

  • Mild (2–5 ng/L): Suppressed fruit, slightly dull; easily mistaken for "closed".
  • Moderate (5–15 ng/L): Clear damp cardboard, cellar, musty notes.
  • 重度 (>15 ng/L): 強烈霉味主導，酒款完全毀壞。

Training Method:

  1. Purchase TCA standard solution (e.g. WineFaults kit).
  2. 在中性白酒中添加 2、5、10、20 ng/L 濃度。
  3. Blind-taste and rank to establish personal threshold curve.
  4. 對比未污染樣品，感受果味壓抑程度。

Misidentification Trap: Mild TCA is often mistaken for "wine too young, needs decanting".

統計: 天然軟木塞污染率 2~5%，螺旋蓋可避免 TCA。

Brettanomyces (Brett)

Chemistry: 4-ethylphenol (4-EP) and 4-ethylguaiacol (4-EG).

Sensory Description:

  • Low concentration (<400 μg/L): Smoky, leather, "wild"; some consider it adds complexity.
  • Moderate concentration (400–800 μg/L): Stable, sweat, plasters.
  • High concentration (>800 μg/L): Faecal, putrid; completely masks fruit.

Regional Controversy:

  • 舊世界: 部分 Rhône、Burgundy 生產者認為低度 Brett 是 terroir 一部分。
  • New World: Most wineries treat it as a fault; strict control (target <200 μg/L).

Training Method:

  1. Compare "clean" Syrah vs Brett-affected Côte-Rôtie.
  2. Use 4-EP standard, adding 200, 500, 1000 μg/L.
  3. Learn to distinguish "positive smoke" (oak) from "negative Brett".

Individual threshold varies widely; establish your own acceptance standard.

Reduction

化學本質: 硫化氫 (H₂S)、甲硫醇、二甲基硫等硫醇化合物。

Sensory Description:

  • Mild: Match-strike, gunpowder, flint (a positive character in some Chablis).
  • Moderate: Rotten egg, burnt rubber, rotting onion.
  • Severe: Sewage, faecal; completely undrinkable.

Dynamic Behaviour:

  • 揮發性: 輕度還原味可透過醒酒或搖杯消散。
  • Irreversible: Severe reduction (mercaptans) cannot be fixed by decanting; requires copper treatment (professional).

Blind Tasting Response:

  1. Initial reductive note → swirl 30 seconds → re-nose.
  2. 若消失: 記錄為「輕度還原 (可醒酒)」，不視為嚴重缺陷。
  3. 若持續: 記錄為「中/重度還原」，扣品質分。

Training: hydrogen sulphide solution (laboratory grade), concentration gradient 1–100 μg/L.

Oxidation

化學本質: 乙醛累積、酚類氧化、顏色轉棕。

Sensory Description:

  • White wine: Apple cider vinegar, caramel, honey, loss of freshness; colour turns golden/brown.
  • Red wine: Stewed fruit, dried figs, leather; tannins soften; colour turns brick/brown.

Normal vs Fault:

Normal oxidative ageingSherry, Tawny Port, Vin Jaune (intentionally oxidative style)
Micro-oxygenationDevelops complexity in red wine ageing (controlled oxidation)
Excessive oxidationPoor sealing, dried cork, improper storage leads to loss of fruit

盲品判斷:

  • If the wine should be fresh (e.g. Sauvignon Blanc) but shows oxidation → fault.
  • If the wine is meant for ageing (e.g. Gran Reserva Rioja) and shows moderate oxidation → normal.

Training: Compare fresh wine vs the same wine deliberately exposed to air for 48 hours.

Fault Quantification and Threshold Testing

  • Threshold Testing: Use ascending concentration series (e.g. 2, 5, 10, 20 ng/L TCA) to determine personal detection threshold.
  • Detection Threshold: The lowest concentration at which "some off-note" is perceived.
  • Recognition Threshold: The concentration at which the fault can be accurately named (typically 2–3× the detection threshold).
  • Individual Variation: TCA thresholds can differ 10-fold; calibrate regularly.

Fault Correction Strategies

FaultPreventionEarly InterventionFinished Wine Correction
TCAAvoid contaminated corksRacking, reverse osmosisIrreversible (replacing stopper is ineffective)
VAHygiene management, SO₂Low temperature, filter acetobacterIrreversible (remove by distillation)
BrettBarrel sanitation, SO₂, filtrationEarly filtrationReverse osmosis, PVPP adsorption
ReductionAdequate oxygen, nutrient supplementationAeration, copper treatmentMild cases dissipate with decanting
OxidationInert gas, low temperatureAdd SO₂Irreversible

slides.7.subtitle: Typicity Matrix
slides.7.title: Chapter 4
slides.8.content:
Typicity Assessment Framework

典型性 (Typicity): 酒款符合其品種/產區/風格預期特徵的程度。

Assessment LevelQuestionEvidence Sources
品種典型性此酒是否展現該品種核心特徵?香氣譜、酸度、單寧結構
Regional TypicityDoes this wine express the terroir of the appellation?Minerality, climate signals, soil characteristics
風格典型性此酒是否符合該風格預期?釀造技術痕跡 (MLF、橡木、陳年)

品種典型性矩陣：紅葡萄

Cabernet Sauvignon Typicity Indicators

Core AromasBlackcurrant, cedar, green pepper (pyrazine), mint
結構高單寧 (粗獷 → 絲滑，視產區)、高酸度、飽滿酒體
Climate SignalsCool: green pepper dominates | Warm: black fruit | Hot: jam, chocolate
Oak IntegrationHigh affinity; vanilla, cedar, smoke prominent
Ageing Potential10–30 years; tannins evolve to silk

Regional Variation:

  • Pauillac: Cedar, pencil shavings, minerality; powerful tannin structure.
  • Napa Valley: 成熟黑果、薄荷、酒精感高 (14.5%+)。
  • Coonawarra: 桉樹、薄荷、Terra Rossa 紅土礦物感。

Blind tasting key: pyrazine (green pepper) is the Cab marker, but excess indicates underripeness.

Pinot Noir Typicity Indicators

Core AromasRed cherry, strawberry, mushroom, wet earth, rose
StructureLow–medium tannins (silky), high acidity, medium to medium-plus body
Climate SignalsCool: red fruit, sharp acidity | Warm: black cherry, jam
Oak IntegrationSubtle; avoid masking delicate fruit; mostly old oak
Ageing Evolution5–15 years; develops forest floor, leather, soy

Regional Variation:

  • Burgundy (Côte d'Or): 紅果、礦物、土壤 (濕土、蘑菇)，高酸。
  • Central Otago: 深色、黑櫻桃、香料、較高酒精。
  • Oregon (Willamette): Between the two; red fruit + earth, medium body.

Blind tasting key: silky tannins + high acidity + red fruit = high-confidence Pinot Noir.

Syrah / Shiraz Typicity Indicators

Core AromasBlackberry, black pepper, smoke, olive, animal
結構中+ ~ 高單寧、中酸度、飽滿酒體
Climate SignalsCool: pepper, olive, smoke | Hot: jam, chocolate, sweet spice
Oak IntegrationGood; smoke, vanilla, mocha
陳年潛力10~25 年，發展皮革、焦油、醬油

Syrah vs Shiraz Style:

CharacteristicSyrah (Cool)Shiraz (Warm)
Key RegionsN. Rhône, South AfricaBarossa, McLaren Vale
香氣黑胡椒、橄欖、煙燻黑莓果醬、巧克力、桉樹
AcidityMed+ to highMed to med+
Alcohol12.5–13.5%14–15.5%

盲品關鍵: 黑胡椒 + 煙燻 = Syrah 標誌，但 Brett 也可能產生類似煙燻。

Regional Typicity Matrix: White Grapes

RegionVarietyCore CharacteristicsKey Differentiators
ChablisChardonnayHigh acidity, mineral (oyster shell, flint), no/minimal oakVery clean, steely acidity
MeursaultChardonnayHazelnut, butter, toast, rich bodyMLF + oak, fuller
MarlboroughSauv. BlancPassionfruit, gooseberry, green pepper, high acidityIntense fruit, clean
SancerreSauv. BlancCitrus, flint, wet stone, herbalMineral-driven, more restrained
MoselRieslingGreen apple, honey, slate, high acidity, low alcoholResidual sugar balance, petrol (aged)
AlsaceRieslingCitrus, floral, drier, higher alcoholFuller, different minerality

盲品推論決策樹

  1. Step 1: Colour and Structure
    • White / rosé / red? → Narrow the variety range.
    • Body light or full? Tannins high or low? → Narrow further.
  2. Step 2: Aroma Family
    • Fruit character (red fruit vs black fruit vs tropical vs citrus)?
    • Herbal / spice / mineral / oak?
  3. Step 3: Climate Signals
    • High acidity + underripe fruit → cool climate.
    • Low acidity + jam + high alcohol → warm climate.
  4. Step 4: Winemaking Technique
    • MLF? 橡木? 酒泥接觸? 全串發酵?
    • Climate + winemaking → identify the appellation.
  5. Step 5: 置信度評估
    • 3+ 個強證據 → 高置信度。
    • 1–2 pieces of evidence → give 2–3 possible appellations.

Common Blind Tasting Traps

TrapFaulty ReasoningCorrect Response
Over-relying on one clueSmells green pepper → must be Cab SauvCheck structure, acidity, and regional logic
Ignoring climate signalsPinot only comes from BurgundyConsider NZ, Oregon, California
Confusing winemaking with varietyButtery → ChardonnayMLF can be used for many varieties
Vintage effect2003 Bordeaux resembles NapaExtreme vintages break conventions
Producer styleSome estates deliberately mimic other regionsFocus on general typicity, not outliers

slides.9.subtitle: Competition Strategy
slides.9.title: Chapter 5
slides.10.content:
Time Management Strategy

RoundTime AllocationKey TasksCommon Mistakes
Round 1 (Scan)2 min / wineQuickly note visual, dominant aromas, structural skeletonOver-detail, dawdling
Round 2 (Deep)3 min / wineFull aroma analysis, palate detail, initial inferenceGetting stuck on one wine
Round 3 (Confirm)1 min / wineVerify inference, fill in missing detailsOver-revising
Summary (10 min)Overall reviewCheck logical consistency, fill gapsPanic-quitting

範例: 12 款酒，總時間 90 分鐘 → 第一輪 24 min、第二輪 36 min、第三輪 12 min、總結 10 min、緩衝 8 min。

Note-Taking System Optimisation

Grid Method

優點: 結構化、易於對比、不遺漏項目。

Design:

ItemWine 1Wine 2Wine 3
AppearanceDeep rubyPale garnetGolden
Aroma IntensityMed+MedPronounced
Dominant AromasBlackcurrant, cedarRed cherry, earthCitrus, honey
AcidityMed+HighHigh
TanninsHighMedN/A
BodyFullMedMed+
Initial InferenceCab PauillacPN BurgRies Mosel

適合需要完整記錄的正式考試 (如 Diploma)。

Shorthand Notation System

Advantages: Fast, space-saving, ideal for competitions.

Common Symbols:

  • Colour: R (red), W (white), Ro (rosé), deep (+), pale (-).
  • Aroma: B (black fruit), R (red fruit), Cit (citrus), Trop (tropical), Oak (oak).
  • Structure: A (acidity), T (tannins), Alc (alcohol), ↑ (high), ↓ (low).
  • Quality: * (good), ** (very good), *** (outstanding).

Example Notes:

酒 1: R深+ | B雪松Oak | A中+ T高↑ | ***Cab Pauillac

酒 2: R淡 | R櫻桃土壤 | A高↑ T中 | **PN Burg

Requires pre-training to build a personal symbol system; revise before the exam.

Mental Map

Advantages: Associative memory, rapid recall, ideal for experienced tasters.

Method:

  1. While tasting, build a mental "reference wine" match.
  2. Example: this wine = 70% typical Pauillac + 30% vintage heat.
  3. Only record key differentiating points (e.g. "riper than standard Pauillac").
  4. Reconstruct the full description during the final summary.

Risk: High memory load; easy to confuse if interrupted.

Requires extensive practice to build a stable "reference wine library" (100+ wines).

Comparative Tasting Techniques

  • 成對對比: 將同品種不同產區酒款並排品評 (如 Burgundy PN vs Oregon PN)。
  • 垂直品評: 同酒款不同年份，學習年份效應與陳年演化。
  • Horizontal Tasting: Same region and vintage, different producers; learn subtle terroir differences.
  • 三角對比: A (標準) vs B (變異 1) vs C (變異 2)，強化區分能力。

Common Competition Question Types

Question TypeChallengeStrategyExample
Classic appellationsMust precisely identify AOCMemorise typicity matrix and village stylesPauillac vs St-Julien
New World mimicsHigh stylistic similarityFocus on climate signals and alcohol levelNapa Cab vs Pauillac
Trap vintagesExtreme vintages break conventionsMemorise key vintage characteristics (2003, 2011)2003 Bordeaux (hot)
Obscure varietiesInsufficient aroma libraryElimination method, structural inferenceNégrette, Timorasso
Fortified/sweet winesWinemaking diversityIdentify oxidative vs non-oxidative, fortification methodPX vs Amontillado

Psychological Pressure Management

  • Expectation Management: Accept that 100% accuracy is impossible; aim for 70–80%.
  • Avoid Anchoring: If the first impression is wrong, be bold enough to overturn and reassess.
  • Time Anxiety: Set midpoint checkpoints (e.g. 5 wines in 30 min); avoid last-minute rushes.
  • Breathing: When sensory fatigue sets in, take 3 deep breaths to reset olfaction.

盲品訓練計畫 (12 週)

WeekThemeTraining ContentNo. of Wines
1–2Variety IdentificationSingle varieties, covering 6 major reds and 6 major whites12 wines × 2 wks
3~4氣候影響同品種不同氣候區 (涼/溫/熱)9 款 × 2 週
5–6Regional TypicityClassic appellation comparisons (France vs New World)12 wines × 2 wks
7–8Winemaking TechniqueOak/MLF/lees/whole-cluster comparisons8 wines × 2 wks
9–10Ageing EvolutionVertical tasting (5–15 years)6 wines × 2 wks
11–12Mock CompetitionMixed question types, timed pressure15 wines × 2 wks

Metacognitive Checklist

Self-questioning after each blind tasting:

  1. 哪些線索是強證據? 哪些是弱證據?
  2. Is my inference logic chain complete? (Colour → Aroma → Structure → Appellation)
  3. Was I affected by any bias? (confirmation bias, anchoring effect)
  4. If wrong, at which step did I go wrong? (perception error vs knowledge gap vs reasoning error)
  5. How to improve? (add knowledge vs train senses vs optimise process)

slides.10.title: Chapter 5: Advanced Blind Tasting Techniques and Competition Strategies
slides.11.content: From neurophysiological mechanisms to competition strategies, this course establishes a systematic sensory evaluation framework. Mastering the calibration protocol (ICC > 0.75), fault quantification (TCA detection threshold 2 ng/L), the typicity matrix (varietal/regional/stylistic triple verification), and time management (three-round tasting method) enables reproducible expert-level blind tasting performance.
slides.11.title: Course Summary
slides.12.questions.0.explanation: Olfactory receptors adapt rapidly; perceived intensity drops 50–70% within 60 seconds, requiring a 3–5 minute rest period to recover baseline sensitivity.
slides.12.questions.0.question: Olfactory adaptation causes perceived intensity to decline by what proportion after 60 seconds of continuous exposure to the same aroma?
slides.12.questions.1.explanation: TCA threshold is extremely low at 2–4 ng/L (ppt level), with individual variation up to 10-fold; regular panel calibration is essential.
slides.12.questions.1.question: What is the typical sensory detection threshold for TCA cork taint?
slides.12.questions.2.explanation: Correct sequence: Colour (narrows variety range) → Aroma (family classification) → Climate signals → Winemaking technique → Confidence assessment.
slides.12.questions.2.question: What is the correct sequence in a blind tasting decision tree?
slides.12.questions.3.explanation: Reference standard solutions allow evaluators to establish reproducible sensory baselines for specific attributes — the gold standard recommended by ISO 13300 for sensory panel calibration.
slides.12.questions.3.options.0: Independent tasting followed by group discussion of differences
slides.12.questions.3.options.1: Reference standard solutions (e.g., tannic acid standards) to establish consensus perception thresholds
slides.12.questions.3.question: During sensory panel calibration training, to ensure evaluators share a consistent perception of "medium-plus tannins", what should be used first?
slides.12.questions.4.explanation: Competitive blind tasting uses a layered elimination approach: confirm variety and climate region (high reliability), then use phenolic development (tannin softening, third-aroma stage) to systematically narrow the vintage range.
slides.12.questions.4.options.0: Guess the most recent vintage to minimise error risk
slides.12.questions.4.options.1: Lock in variety and climate zone first, then use acidity and phenolic evolution to narrow the vintage window
slides.12.questions.4.options.2: Abandon vintage estimation entirely and focus on describing aromatic complexity
slides.12.questions.4.question: In a high-level blind tasting competition, facing a wine with clear ageing potential but an uncertain vintage, what is the most effective strategy?
